subject: Packaging options, upgrade/downgrade flexibility and feature-credit structure for HealthMate
messages:
From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@healthmate.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 08:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Packaging options and upgrade/downgrade flexibility

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the team at HealthMate was impressed with the latency numbers. We have two quick follow-ups from procurement as we prep an internal recommendation:

1) If we commit to the Compact tier with a 12-month reserved capacity, what is the upgrade path to the Elastic tier mid-contract? Any proration rules or credits when moving up?
2) Conversely, if we need to step down at month 9 (usage lower than forecast), what downgrade options or credit protections exist?
3) Can you outline how feature bundles work in practice? We want to ensure the Clinical Reranker and Dedicated KV Cache are available as add-ons, and whether bundling them with seats yields a better unit price.

Can you send a short one-pager or spreadsheet that shows (a) Net effective price at typical usage bands, (b) proration on upgrades/downgrades, and (c) any one-off setup credits or promotional discounts? Procurement asked for a clear example so they can include it in the SOW.

Appreciate it — copying contracts@healthmate.com for visibility.

Best,
Sara Liu
Director of Platform Partnerships
HealthMate

Attachment: none

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@healthmate.com>, contracts@healthmate.com
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging options and upgrade/downgrade flexibility

Hi Sara — great to meet you and the team. Short answers below and I attached a spreadsheet with example scenarios.

- Upgrade path (Compact -> Elastic): We allow mid-term upgrades. Usage is recalculated monthly; you pay the delta between Compact committed price and Elastic committed price pro-rated from the upgrade effective date. We also offer a one-time migration credit equal to 10% of the remaining Compact commitment if you move to Elastic within the first 6 months.

- Downgrade (step down): Downgrades can be scheduled to take effect at the next billing cycle. If you reduce committed capacity before month 12, there's a 30-day notice plus an early step-down fee equal to the prorated difference capped at 20% of the remaining term, unless you convert unused committed units into a credit for Redwood Optimize consulting time.

- Feature bundling: Clinical Reranker and Dedicated KV Cache can be purchased as standalone add-ons. Bundling them with seat blocks (e.g., 50+ seats) unlocks a 12% bundle discount on add-on list prices and may qualify you for a 5% platform credit. The attached "HealthMate_Pricing_Proposal_v3.xlsx" shows three scenarios (low/medium/high usage) with unit economics.

I also included a draft SOW (SOW-HealthMate-draft.pdf) that you can drop into procurement. If helpful, I can put together a mutual action plan and proposed milestone-based credits.

Next step: Are you available Monday for a 20-minute call to walk procurement through the spreadsheet?

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: HealthMate_Pricing_Proposal_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet), SOW-HealthMate-draft.pdf (pdf)

From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@healthmate.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com, contracts@healthmate.com
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging options and upgrade/downgrade flexibility

Thanks Aditya — the spreadsheet is helpful. A couple of clarifying items from procurement:

- That 10% migration credit sounds promising. Is it stackable with an intro discount for new customers?
- For the downgrade fee: can HealthMate convert unused committed units to a token bank (platform credits) that expire after 12 months instead of paying the fee? That would be preferred.
- Do you have standard language for the proration rules we can paste into the SOW (procurement wants explicit math for month-of-change billing).

If you can share those details, we'll loop legal and aim to have comments back by Wednesday.

Cheers,
Sara

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: Packaging options and upgrade/downgrade flexibility — approval for migration credit and bundle discount?

Grace / Marissa,

Looping you both for a quick approval path and pricing guidance. HealthMate (Sara Liu) has asked whether the 10% migration credit is stackable with a new-customer intro discount and whether we can convert unused committed units into a 12-month token bank instead of charging the step-down fee. Quick summary (from the spreadsheet):

- Proposed: 10% migration credit (applies if upgrade to Elastic within 6 months).
- Bundle: 12% off add-ons + 5% platform credit when bundled with 50+ seats.
- Step-down: Standard is 30-day notice + early step-down fee capped at 20% of remaining term. HealthMate prefers conversion to 12-month platform credits.

Request: Can we approve stacking the 10% migration credit with a one-time 7% intro discount (total 17% effective) for first-year committed spend? Also, can we offer conversion of unused units to a platform credit that expires after 12 months (instead of the fee) — this would be revenue-neutral if we limit conversion to up to 30% of the committed units and apply a 10% conversion admin fee.

I'll be on the Monday call with Sara to walk procurement through the spreadsheet. Need a response by Monday 10:00 PT so I can close on the call.

Thanks,
Aditya

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Packaging options and upgrade/downgrade flexibility — approval for migration credit and bundle discount?

Aditya — thanks for the clear ask. I agree with a constrained version of what you proposed. Approval notes below (copy to legal & finance as needed):

- Stacking: Approve stacking the 10% migration credit with a one-time 7% intro discount for net-effective concessions on year 1 only. Add note in SOW: "Intro discount applies to committed platform fees only; migration credit applied to the remaining Compact commitment balance at time of upgrade."

- Conversion option: Approve conversion of unused committed units into a 12-month platform credit instead of the early step-down fee, subject to conditions:
  * Conversion capped at 30% of total committed units for the term.
  * 10% administrative conversion charge applied to converted units.
  * Credits expire 12 months after issuance and are non-refundable.

- Bundles: Approve 12% add-on bundle discount and the 5% platform credit for bundles >=50 seats. Finance asks that any crediting flow through the billing system as line-item credits (not as an upfront discount) so we can track retention impact.

Please work with legal to add the explicit proration math snippet. Also capture the HubSpot deal update (HLTH-8421) with the approved concessions. I'll loop in Marissa for SOW clean-up.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
